challenges.title: Design Challenge for the National Fallen Highway Workers Memorial
prizes: The winning design is featured on official DOT communication platforms
challenges.summary: Designs for a memorial to highway workers killed in work zones, either a mobile exhibit (Track A) or a permanent indoor piece at DOT (Track B), with a plan and a cost estimate of no more than $50,000. Entries go by email to WZMemorial@dot.gov; any use of AI tools must be disclosed.

challenges.title: AHRQ Healthcare Choice and Competition Challenge
challenges.sponsor: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality
prizes: Up to $11.8 million in total prizes: up to $3 million in Phase 1 and up to $8.8 million in Phase 2
challenges.summary: Research projects on regulatory, financial, organizational or delivery reforms that strengthen competition, lower prices and widen access in healthcare. Up to five Phase 1 winners; only they go on to Phase 2. AHRQ invites individuals, teams, academic institutions and other U.S.-based entities.

challenges.title: NASA TechLeap Prize: Orbital Clarity Challenge
prizes: Up to $2 million in total prizes: up to four winners, each up to $500,000 across three phases
Non-cash prize: a no-cost flight test for each winning team
challenges.summary: Low-cost ways to measure thermospheric density, pressure or drag in low Earth orbit. Phase 1 registration closes October 28, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET; Phase 1 submissions close November 11, 2026.

challenges.title: 2026 NIH Prize for Excellence in Disability Health Research
challenges.sponsor: National Institutes of Health, Disability Health Research Program
prizes: Total cash prizes: $300,000 (up to three $100,000 prizes, for an early-stage, a midcareer and a senior investigator)
challenges.summary: Recognizes investigators for outstanding, collaborative contributions to disability health research, including work that involves disabled people from study design through dissemination.

challenges.title: 2027 NIA Start-Up Challenge and Accelerator
prizes: Stage 1: up to 21 finalists, $24,000 each and a place in an entrepreneurial accelerator
challenges.summary: Early-stage ventures in aging research compete for cash and a place in an accelerator. Individual winners and team leads must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents; entities must be incorporated and based in the U.S.

challenges.title: Advancing the Inclusion of People with Disabilities in Clinical Research Challenge
challenges.sponsor: National Institutes of Health, Disability Health Research Program
prizes: Total cash prizes: $1,000,000 (up to twenty $50,000 prizes)
challenges.summary: NIH prize for practices that include people with disabilities in clinical research; it closes on the same day as the NIH disability health research prize.

challenges.title: NASA Lunar Grounding Challenge
challenges.summary: Ways to safely and quickly discharge the static charge an astronaut's suit builds up during moonwalks at the lunar south pole, before touching the lander.

challenges.title: SPARK PubMed/PMC Challenge (Semantic Precision for AI Retrieval of Knowledge)
prizes: Two tasks (known-item retrieval; open-ended questions answered with citations), each $100,000 for first place and $25,000 for second
challenges.summary: AI systems that find and cite biomedical evidence in a PubMed/PMC corpus. Registration closes January 2, 2027; the scored challenge runs January 15 to February 1, 2027. Open to individuals, teams, companies, academic institutions and nonprofits.

challenges.title: SPARK dbGaP Challenge (Semantic Precision for AI Retrieval of Knowledge)
prizes: Two tasks (mapping study variables to ontology concepts; conversational cohort feasibility), each $100,000 for first place and $25,000 for second
challenges.summary: AI systems that map dbGaP study variables to standard ontology concepts and help researchers judge cohort feasibility from public metadata. Registration closes January 2, 2027; the scored challenge runs January 15 to February 1, 2027.

challenges.title: NASA's Human Lander Challenge (HuLC)
challenges.summary: NASA's Human Lander Challenge (HuLC) invites collegiate teams to develop innovative systems-level solutions to understand, establish, and optimize lunar communications systems. The systems will be for landers and surface level operations and will be implemented in 3 to 5 years.

challenges.title: AHRQ Clinical Evidence Synthesis Transformation Challenge
challenges.sponsor: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality
prizes: Total cash prizes: up to $5.85 million
Phase 1: up to five finalists, $100,000 each
challenges.summary: Part of AHRQ's Super Intelligence for Healthcare Improvement Initiative: AI systems that cut medical evidence synthesis from a year or more to hours, judged on accuracy, throughput, reproducibility, usability and ease of operation. Open to individuals, teams and for-profit and nonprofit entities.
